lines.watchItem: Merchant-GPU demand runs very hot, with a record NVDA data-center quarter, hyperscaler capex climbing about 77%, and a 3.6M-unit B200 backlog signaling booked leading-edge wafer demand years out. Watch whether that demand holds if capex jitters spread.

Advanced packaging is the binding limit: CoWoS is sold out through 2027 on 52-78 week leads and HBM is sold out for 2026, so packaging, not wafers, caps realizable GPU revenue. Watch the ramp from about 75K toward 125-130K wafers a month.

The packaging gap is set to narrow from about 20% to 10% by end-2026 as two packaging suppliers add CoWoS capacity, pushing total supply toward roughly 200K wafers a month with outside packaging partners. Watch whether added capacity loosens allocation or just meets rising demand.

Custom ASICs are growing faster than merchant GPUs (44.6% vs 16.1%) and already run about two-thirds of AI compute, while Broadcom and Marvell control roughly 95% of that co-design. TSMC's leading-node base tilts toward hyperscaler custom silicon routed through two design houses.

The top three CoWoS clients take over 85% of capacity, with NVDA near 60% and AMD near 11% that AMD splits between its server processors and its accelerators. TSMC's advanced-packaging revenue leans on one dominant buyer.

Pricing stays firm across the chain, with TSMC's Q2 gross margin at 67.7% up 9.1 points, NVDA holding 70-80% share and pricing power, and HBM4 prices set to roughly double into 2027. Watch how much of that pricing power TSMC keeps versus what flows to memory suppliers.

Competitive and policy moves are stirring: Intel is expanding Intel-3 in Ireland and pitching a Crescent Island part that skips CoWoS and HBM, while NVDA's China revenue halved to $4.55B under export limits. Watch whether route-around designs or policy shifts move foundry demand.
